description: Routing and capability manifest for Design Fleet. The CLI and website preview relevance and invocation eligibility; native hosts select skills from their supported metadata. This preview is not runtime enforcement.

design-contract.description: Own the project's design truth in five modes: setup writes a requested taste profile at the selected host path; assess rates codebase design consistency; draft generates a filled VISION.md hard-rails contract; reconcile diffs the doc against reality; plan turns FEEDBACK.md and the north star into proposed Goals rows

setup.precondition: User requests setup or accepts a setup offer; reuse an existing profile and preserve its owner-defined preferences.

not_this_skill.when: user wants to build UI
user wants a visual critique, Nielsen heuristic review, or to verify just-generated code
taste profile already exists and user only wants to review it
user wants a deep motion-only audit with leverage-ranked findings and executor plans
not_this_skill.use: motion-audit (assess covers the whole design surface at rating altitude)

frontend-design.description: Build, fix or polish UI, small fixes included. Use when something feels janky, slow, laggy or dead when pressed, the page jumps sideways, spacing feels off, or someone asks to add dark mode, an empty state, a menu, dropdown, modal, command palette or tooltip, a transition or animation between states or pages, a layout that works on phones, or to make it feel like Linear or another product. Also covers easing, springs, reduced motion, drag and gestures, scrollbars, colour and contrast, UI copy, and Next.js and Tailwind setup. Points each job to the one reference to read before editing. Use design-review to critique or review UI, design-contract for VISION.md and project-wide consistency, and animation-vocabulary to name an effect.
triggers: can't catch it while it moves
help me decide how this should animate

not_this_skill.when: user wants to review existing UI quality, run a Nielsen heuristic review, or verify the just-built code follows the rules
user wants a codebase audit, a project VISION.md, or a taste profile
user wants several genuinely different versions to flip through and pick from
not_this_skill.use: proto (explicit /proto invocation only — point the user at it)

not_this_skill.when: user wants a codebase-wide motion audit producing executor plans
not_this_skill.use: motion-audit (explicit /motion-audit invocation only — point the user at it)

not_this_skill.when: user asks where motion would help or what should animate here
bare accessibility/a11y requests about focus, ARIA, contrast, or hit targets (not motion)
not_this_skill.use: frontend-design interaction-design reference + color-contrast/ux-laws rules — not a motion surface

design-review.description: Two-altitude evaluator of existing UI. Deterministic floor (formerly design-lint): validates code against grep-able check IDs and the VISION.md contract via `design-fleet lint`, producing a pass/fail report. Subjective ceiling (formerly design-critique): a systematic visual + behavioral critique of a screenshot, file, or URL, with a formal Nielsen review (references/nielsen-review.md) on explicit request, and a motion opportunity scan (references/motion-opportunities.md, explicit request only) that proposes the few places motion would genuinely improve existing UI — with exact values — and names what should stay static
triggers: did I follow the design rules
does this pass the design rules
design-review.output_notes: Report executable checks, agent review, and rendered interaction evidence separately. Executable coverage is limited to the shipped check registry and activated contract checks. Ordinary critique is advisory; a subjective score gates only under explicit project policy and current independent calibration. The CLI does not promote agent goals from critique history.
design-review.precondition: code or a visual artifact exists to review

not_this_skill.when: user wants to build new UI from scratch (or a motion/pattern implementation)
user wants a full codebase audit, to draft/reconcile VISION.md, or to set up a taste profile
user wants accepted motion opportunities implemented
user wants a codebase-wide motion audit with per-finding executor plans
user wants one animation decided before it exists

animation-vocabulary.description: Names a motion effect from a loose description. Use when someone asks what an effect is called, such as what do you call it, what's the name for it, or the word for an animation, transition or effect. Carries the fleet's house terms and links the full motion glossary. Naming only; frontend-design builds the effect and design-review judges one.
triggers: how do I describe this animation

not_this_skill.when: user wants the effect designed or implemented
user wants an existing animation judged or improved

motion-audit.description: Codebase-wide motion audit: map the motion, 8-category audit, vetted leverage-ranked findings, then self-contained executor plans in plans/motion/NNN-*.md with their index in plans/motion/README.md. Read-only on source code; execute changes source only after the person says yes, and never commits. Explicit invocation only (disable-model-invocation)
triggers: audit the animations in this codebase

not_this_skill.when: user wants a diff or one component's motion reviewed
user wants the whole design surface audited or VISION work
user wants it fixed now
user wants proposals for where to ADD motion

proto.description: Builds 3-5 genuinely divergent, fully working variants of one UI piece behind a copied switcher (switcher.js); the user flips live and picks. keep integrates the winner with the existing components and tokens, deletes the prototype with rm -r and records the decision in FEEDBACK.md. Never touches production during exploration. Explicit invocation only (disable-model-invocation)

not_this_skill.when: user wants one committed build
user wants project-level taste elicitation
user wants shipped UI judged

figma-absorb.description: Absorbs a Figma file's design system — local and subscribed-library variable collections, read-only — into one self-contained HTML reference: live swatches painted by the tokens, a mode switcher, alias chains to endpoints, descriptions, origin badges, and a findings appendix. Never writes to Figma. Explicit invocation only.
triggers: figma variables to a reference document
figma-absorb.precondition: Explicit invocation and Figma's official MCP read tools (whoami, get_libraries, search_design_system, get_metadata, get_variable_defs). use_figma only for a read-only fallback the person asks for, after loading figma-use; such a run is read-only by intent, not provable. Library imports are mutations and are never made; unreadable values are reported as unavailable.

not_this_skill.when: user wants tokens.css/tokens.json for code consumption with verified baselines
not_this_skill.use: a sync pipeline — out of this skill's scope by design

not_this_skill.when: user wants UI built from the absorbed tokens
user wants the absorbed map turned into project hard rails
not_this_skill.use: design-contract (draft); this skill proposes values for the existing token-table slots and never writes them

not_this_skill.when: user wants anything written INTO the Figma file
not_this_skill.use: nothing in the fleet — this skill is read-only by cardinal rule

routing_notes.advisory: This section describes workflow boundaries. Preview scores indicate relevance, not host invocation. Explicit-only utilities are ineligible for automatic selection. Native hosts enforce their own supported invocation metadata.
priority_order: If the request names an effect ("what do you call it when...", "what's the name for..."): animation-vocabulary
If the user requests a taste profile or accepts a setup offer → design-contract (setup mode); a missing profile does not interrupt other work
If input is a screenshot or image → design-review
If request mentions Nielsen, heuristics, or formal usability → design-review (references/nielsen-review.md)
If request is to audit/scan the codebase, draft/reconcile the VISION.md contract, or set up a taste profile → design-contract
If request is to lint, validate, or verify generated code against design rules or the contract → design-review
If request is to critique, review, or improve a specific visual artifact → design-review
If request asks where motion would help / what should animate (explicit scan) → design-review (references/motion-opportunities.md)

The three utilities never auto-route: /motion-audit (codebase motion audit → plans), /proto (divergent variants → live picker), and /figma-absorb (Figma design system → live reference document) fire only on explicit invocation — surface them when the request matches, do not select them
Otherwise (build UI, or a motion/easing/pattern question) → frontend-design (the fallback)
routing_notes.composable: Skills can chain. Greenfield: design-contract (draft) → frontend-design → design-review; setup is optional and a missing taste profile never blocks work. Existing project: design-contract (assess) → design-contract (draft VISION.md) → design-fleet inventory → frontend-design → design-review. Component work: components table in VISION.md → frontend-design (extend the canonical file) → design-review with render evidence. Maintenance: design-contract (reconcile) when the contract drifts from reality. Motion maintenance: /motion-audit → plans → execution → design-review (references/motion-review.md); undecided direction: /proto → promotion → frontend-design conventions. Design-system intake: /figma-absorb → design-contract (draft token map) → frontend-design → design-review.
